tagline: Leading global designer and manufacturer of pool equipment, outdoor living products and industrial flow control solutions
hero_kpi_rationale: HAYW's key metric: 85% of sales come from aftermarket (replacement, upgrades), a recurring and resilient model, very different from pure-play hardware. This is the company's true structural driver.

kpis.name: Aftermarket Sales Mix
kpis.explanation: Percentage of sales related to replacement or upgrade of existing equipment.
kpis.description: This KPI is central: it shows growth is driven by existing homeowners modernizing their pools, not just new construction.
kpis.signal: Strong recurring model: 85% of sales come from aftermarket.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Margin between sales and cost of production.
kpis.description: Gross margin improves due to favorable pricing and operational gains, despite inflation.
kpis.signal: 170 bps improvement driven by price increases and efficiency gains.

kpis.name: Op Margin
kpis.description: Operating margin reaches 20.8% in 2025, driven by revenue growth and expense control.
kpis.signal: Operating margin rising, supported by growth and cost management.

kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Total sales after deductions and discounts.
kpis.description: Revenue reaches $1.122B in 2025, up 6.7%, driven by price increases and the ChlorKing acquisition.
kpis.signal: Solid organic growth of 6.7%, driven by pricing and acquisitions.

kpis.name: R&D (% of Revenue)
kpis.description: R&D spending remains stable at 2.4% of revenue, focused on connected and sustainable products.
kpis.signal: Stable investment in innovation, centered on IoT and energy-efficient products.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Operating result adjusted for non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA reaches $299.3M, up 7.9%, supported by gross margin gains despite higher overheads.
kpis.signal: Adjusted EBITDA growth exceeds revenue growth, indicating cost leverage.

kpis.name: NAM Sales Mix
kpis.explanation: Percentage of sales generated in North America.
kpis.description: North America accounts for 85% of total sales, a stable ratio over the past two years.
kpis.signal: Core business remains highly concentrated in North America.

kpis.name: Price Impact on Growth
kpis.explanation: Portion of sales growth attributable to price increases.
kpis.description: In 2025, 5.4% of sales growth comes from price increases, implemented to offset inflation and tariffs.
kpis.signal: Price increases contributed 5.4 pts of growth, offsetting inflation.

risks.title: Competition
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in markets with high levels of competition, which may pressure profit margins and limit its ability to maintain or grow market share.

risks.title: New Product Development
risks.score_rationale: The company's future success depends on its ability to develop, manufacture, and market new products, which involves significant risks.

risks.title: Technological Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company must keep pace with rapid technological developments, including artificial intelligence, to remain competitive.

risks.title: Reputational Damage
risks.score_rationale: Damage to the company's reputation could lead to loss of customer and supplier trust, as well as significant financial losses.

risks.title: Supply Chain Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company relies on suppliers to obtain components and materials necessary for product manufacturing.

risks.title: Economic Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to economic risks, including market fluctuations and changes in economic conditions.

risks.title: Regulatory Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to regulations and laws that may change and affect its operations.

risks.title: Cybersecurity Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to cybersecurity risks, including cyberattacks and data breaches.

ai_positioning.summary: HAYW recognizes the importance of keeping pace with rapid technological developments, including artificial intelligence, to remain competitive. However, no active AI applications or deployments are documented in current operations. AI-related risk is identified as a strategic area of focus.
evidence: Item 1A Risk Factors: Our ability to keep pace with evolving technologies, including AI, and effectively develop and deploy such technologies.
